test_title: RRB ALP CBT-II (Heat Engine) Official Paper (Held On: 02 May, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: What is the main difference between a double piston with step bore and a double piston with straight bore wheel cylinder?

options.text: The step bore operates without hydraulic pressure.
The step bore uses a single piston.
The step bore does not use brake shoes.
The step bore has pistons with different diameters.

solution:
The correct answer is __The step bore has pistons with different diameters.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Step bore wheel cylinders__ are designed with pistons of varying diameters.
 
• The smaller piston helps in reducing braking force required at lower speeds, enhancing braking control.
 
• The larger piston provides increased braking force for higher speeds, ensuring effective braking when needed.
 
• This design improves the overall efficiency and functionality of the braking system.
 
• The step bore design is commonly used in modern vehicles to balance performance and safety.
 
• In contrast, a straight bore wheel cylinder features pistons of the same diameter, leading to uniform braking force distribution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Hydraulic Braking System:**

 
 
• A hydraulic braking system uses brake fluid to transfer force from the brake pedal to the brake mechanisms at each wheel.
 
• It ensures smooth and consistent braking performance.
 
 
 
• **Drum Brake:**
 
 
• Drum brakes use brake shoes that press outward against a spinning drum to create friction.
 
• They are commonly used on rear wheels of vehicles.
 
 
 
• **Disc Brake:**
 
 
• Disc brakes use brake pads that clamp onto a spinning rotor to create friction and slow the vehicle.
 
• They provide better heat dissipation and are often used on front wheels of vehicles.
